Treat uint8, not int8, indices as masks in meta_index_Tensor (#201374)

## Linked issue or supporting maintainer

Fixes #200546
Part of #201370
Supported by @ezyang

## BC-breaking?

No. Eager already rejects int8 index tensors (and other dtypes besides long,
int, uint8 and bool); under fake tensors / meta, `index` treated int8 as a
boolean mask and `index_put` accepted any index dtype. Both now raise
IndexError like eager, so torch.compile of e.g. `x[int8_index] = v` fails at
trace time instead of in the eager fallback. uint8 masks, which eager accepts (with
a deprecation warning), are no longer rejected for their dtype under fake
tensors / meta; they take the same mask expansion path as bool masks, so
torch.compile graph-breaks on them instead of failing. Under torch.compile on
GPU, `index_put_` with a uint8 mask and a CPU scalar value now fails like it
does in eager ("masked_fill_ only supports boolean masks") instead of
succeeding.

## Summary (human written only)

There appears to be an existing latent bug in the meta implementation for uint8/int8. This bug is in semantics for a index type that we are deprecating anyway, but it simplifies the later PR to fix this bug first before we deprecate.

## Agent details (if applicable)

> `meta_index_Tensor` mirrors `checkIndexTensorTypes` / `expandTensors`, but
> checked `torch.int8` where those check `kByte` (uint8). As a result it
> accepted int8 indices and expanded them as masks, while eager raises
> "tensors used as indices must be long, int, byte or bool tensors"; and it
> rejected uint8 masks, which eager expands, so `torch.compile` of
> `x[uint8_mask]` failed with a fake tensor error. Check uint8 instead of
> int8, and raise IndexError like eager.
>
> The `index_put` / `index_put_` / `_unsafe_index_put` metas didn't check
> index dtypes at all; they now share the same `checkIndexTensorTypes` mirror.
>
> Two other mirrors of the same check made the same mistake and are fixed too:
>
> - The fake tensor dispatch cache bypasses `aten.index.Tensor` for indices
>   that `meta_index_Tensor` calls nonzero on; it checked int8.
> - Inductor's `is_index_put_and_requires_h2d_sync_for_gpu_value` keeps a CPU
>   scalar value on the CPU when eager `index_put_` would dispatch to
>   `masked_fill_` (`canDispatchToMaskedFill` accepts kBool and kByte); it
>   checked int8, so for uint8 masks it moved the value to the GPU.
>
> Not changed here: beyond index dtypes, the fake / meta indexing kernels
> don't reproduce all of eager's error handling, and that predates this PR.
> For example, they don't take eager's masked_fill_ fast path in `index_put`
> (so a uint8 mask with a one-element CPU value traces, while eager fails in
> masked_fill_), they check mask shapes after calling nonzero, and
> `_unsafe_index` shares `index`'s meta although eager only accepts long and
> int indices for it. Aligning those is a separate change.
>
> uint8 masks become an error in eager and meta later in this stack
> (#201370).
>
> Test plan: `python test/test_fake_tensor.py
> TestFakeTensorDispatchCache.test_cache_aten_index`, which asserted the old
> int8-as-mask behavior and now also checks that uint8 masks bypass the cache
> like bool masks; `TestFakeTensor.test_index_tensor_types_match_eager` (new:
> index / index_put / index_put_ / _unsafe_index_put with int8, int16 and
> float indices raise the same IndexError under fake tensors as in eager);
> `pytest test/inductor/test_move_constructors_to_gpu.py -k index_put_mask`
> (new; checks the predicate on hand-built graphs, CPU-only, but the file
> runs in GPU CI); test_indexing.py under PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_DYNAMO=1
> (test_byte_mask failed when uint8 raised IndexError from meta, which
> dynamo propagates instead of falling back to eager).
>
> Authored with an AI assistant.

[CPP FakeTensor] Track C++ fakes in non-strict export leak detection (#200134)

Non-strict export leak detection records fakes from FakeTensor.__init__,
which C++ fakes never run. They are now also recorded in set_proxy_slot,
where every tensor registered with a tracer passes: proxy_call outputs,
higher-order op outputs (which HOPs register through track_tensor_tree, not
proxy_call), placeholders, and sub-tracers. That traversal already happens,
so this adds no extra walk over op outputs. Both call sites go through a new
track_fake_tensor_for_export helper, which records only while exporting with
detect_non_strict_fake_tensor_leaks.

An alternative was to record outputs in proxy_call, but that misses HOP
outputs and adds a traversal of every op's outputs. Recording C++ fakes when
they are created, mirroring __init__, would match Python exactly, but needs a
callback from C++ fake creation into Python. Compared with __init__, the
set_proxy_slot approach misses a fake created while proxy tracing is disabled,
and does not report the fakes a HOP creates internally to trace its branches,
which Python currently reports as leaks even when nothing leaked.

This also catches Python fakes that __init__ does not record because they
are created before tracking starts: _fakify_module_inputs fakifies the
parameters of an nn.Module input before is_exporting() is set, and
set_proxy_slot records them when tracing registers them. Every other Python
fake created during non-strict export already goes through __init__.

A tensor can now be recorded more than once (by __init__ and set_proxy_slot,
or again when an in-place op re-registers it), which the WeakSet tracker
cannot handle: re-adding creates a new weakref with the same hash, set lookup
compares the two weakrefs, which compares the referents with Tensor.__eq__,
and bool() of that elementwise result fails. The tracker becomes a
WeakIdKeyDictionary (identity-keyed, values unused), and
find_legit_leaks_from_referrers returns a list instead of a WeakSet. The input
is already deduplicated by identity and the caller only iterates and checks
len(), so a list is sufficient. find_legit_leaks_from_referrers takes and
returns Tensors, since the tracker only records values that pass
is_fake_tensor. With the old WeakSet, 5 of the 6 existing leak
tests fail on the double recording.

test_detect_leak_nonstrict_module_input_param leaks a parameter of an
nn.Module input, which only set_proxy_slot records, and checks that the
reported tensor is that parameter (node m_linear_weight). The input is the
module-level InputModule because test_serdes.py reruns the test with
save/load, which pickles the module input's class.

No test covers HOP outputs or C++ fakes. HOP outputs are Python fakes at this
point in the stack, which FakeTensor.__init__ already records, so a HOP test
would pass without this change; and non-strict export always uses a Python
FakeTensorMode here, so no test can exercise C++ fakes.

Test Plan:

```
python test/export/test_export.py -k test_detect_leak -k test_function_holding_tensor -k test_export_cyclic_reference_leak
python test/export/test_serdes.py -k test_detect_leak_nonstrict_module_input_param
lintrunner torch/_subclasses/fake_tensor.py torch/fx/experimental/proxy_tensor.py torch/export/_leakage_detection_utils.py torch/export/_trace.py test/export/test_export.py
```

These were run from this stack's test file against a faketensor-cpp build,
with that build's tracking replaced by this change's. All 7 pass with Python
FakeTensor, as do test_detect_leak_nonstrict_module_input_param's variants in
test_serdes.py, test_retraceability.py, test_export_training_ir_to_run_decomp.py,
test_cpp_serdes.py, test_export_strict.py and test_strict_export_v2.py; without the set_proxy_slot
call, test_detect_leak_nonstrict_module_input_param fails, and it also fails
if the forward leaks m.linear.bias instead.

Avoid symbolic storage recomputation on FakeTensor cache hits (#192047)

Relates to pytorch/pytorch#191500

## Problem

FakeTensor's dispatch cache stores a recipe for rebuilding an output, not the output itself. On every cache hit, the old code rebuilt all strided outputs with `empty_strided`; views then rebound that placeholder to the current input with `set_`. For dynamic shapes, both general operations repeatedly calculate symbolic storage bounds.

## Change

This PR uses simpler, equivalent reconstruction for the two common cases:

| Cached output | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh, canonical-contiguous output | `empty_strided(shape, stride)` | `empty(shape)` |
| Cached same-dtype view of an input | `empty_strided(...)` then `set_(input storage, ...)` | `as_strided(input, ...)` |
| Anything else | existing fallback | unchanged |

For example, cached `clone(x)` with symbolic shape `(s, 8)` changes from `empty_strided((s, 8), (8, 1))` to `empty((s, 8))`. Cached `x.transpose(0, 1)` changes from allocating and rebinding a placeholder to `as_strided(x, (8, s), (1, 8), 0)`, directly constructing a view of the current input.

Dtype-changing views such as `view_as_real` retain the typed-placeholder plus `set_` path because `as_strided` cannot change dtype. Fresh noncontiguous outputs also retain `empty_strided`.

The direct `as_strided` path also deliberately changes one edge case: if a FakeTensor input's storage was resized to zero, a cached view now keeps that zero-sized storage. The old placeholder plus `set_` reconstruction grew the storage to cover the view, while an uncached FakeTensor view keeps it at zero. Matching the uncached result is important because AOTAutograd uses zero-sized FakeTensor storage to represent resized storage. I reflected this as [a regression test](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/192047/changes#diff-3bc0cf540b694f4ec0a3749f78b047456657a53a5657e495ffb68e5970c5fdaaR3822).

Canonical-contiguous detection requires structurally identical symbolic stride expressions, rather than expressions that are only provably value-equal. This preserves input SymNode identity in cache entries. Views that require gradients continue to use the existing placeholder path.

## Performance

Measured with [`qwen3_compile_repro.py`](https://gist.github.com/zou3519/63fa2e77d7fcefe21c73d44e4e9190d6/3f1b7df41dbcd53c390f657d480aec048520d70a) on `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`, an NVIDIA H100 (Hopper, `sm_90`), and CUDA 13.4. Three interleaved fresh processes per arm used separate Inductor caches.

| Metric | Base median | Patch median | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Static first call | 38.876 s | 38.786 s | -0.2% |
| Dynamic first call | 56.872 s | 49.673 s | -12.7% |
| Dynamic `aot_collect_metadata` | 5.244 s | 3.561 s | -32.1% |

After each timed first call, an untimed second shape reused the same compiled graph.

## Tests

- `python test/test_fake_tensor.py -k FakeTensorDispatchCache` (42 passed)
- `python test/test_dynamic_shapes.py -k test_unbacked_reshape2` (1 passed)
- Dynamic `torch.compile` integration check: eager parity, zero graph breaks, and one graph reused across two shapes

[FakeTensor] Propagate backend metadata through fake tensor conversion (#186324)

Backends that attach `c10::BackendMeta` to a tensor (via the PrivateUse1
backend-metadata mechanism, the same one used for `torch.save` / `torch.load`)
currently lose that metadata when the tensor is converted to a `FakeTensor`.
`FakeTensorConverter.from_real_tensor` builds the fake tensor from a fresh meta
tensor and never copies `backend_meta_`, so any backend relying on it (e.g.
PrivateUse1) sees it dropped under `torch.compile` / fake tensor propagation.

This adds `torch._C._copy_backend_meta(src, dst)`, a small helper in
`pickler_helper.h` alongside `get`/`setTensorMetadata`, that clones the source
tensor's `c10::BackendMeta` onto the destination via `BackendMeta::clone()` and
leaves all other tensor metadata untouched (it is a no-op when the source has no
backend metadata). `from_real_tensor` then calls it so the fake tensor retains
the real tensor's backend metadata.

Unlike routing through `get`/`setTensorMetadata`, the clone-based copy moves the
full `BackendMeta` object rather than a `Dict[str, bool]` projection, and does
not depend on the tensor's reported device — so it is correct regardless of
`FakeTensorMode.in_kernel_invocation`.

Test Plan:

```bash

python test/cpp_extensions/open_registration_extension/torch_openreg/tests/test_storage.py -k test_fake_tensor_metadata_preservation
python test/cpp_extensions/open_registration_extension/torch_openreg/tests/test_compile.py -k test_backend_metadata_propagation
```

[CPP FakeTensor] Factor real-tensor propagation into shared Python helpers (#199784)

The C++ Fake fallback needs the same propagate_real_tensors behavior as Python
FakeTensorMode: run the op on the real tensors before any fake kernel, then
cross-check and attach the reals to the fake outputs, and infer a fake kernel
from the real output for custom ops that lack one. Move that logic out of
FakeTensorMode._dispatch_impl into module-level helpers and have
_dispatch_impl call them, so both paths share one implementation:

- run_real_op returns a RealOpResult (or None when propagation is skipped);
  _dispatch_impl's inline real-op block and its SKIPPED log move here.
- propagate_real_tensors is the body of maybe_propagate_real_tensors,
  built on the per-tensor propagate_real_tensor.
- can_infer_fake_from_real_out / infer_fake_from_real_out cover
  missing-fake-kernel inference, used both directly and when a
  profile-generated fake kernel raises MissingOpProfile.
- torch._library.fake_impl.run_fake_impl runs a register_fake kernel,
  returning NotImplemented when there is none.

Behavior is unchanged for Python FakeTensorMode. The differences:

- The helpers accept C++ fakes as well as Python FakeTensors, which is what
  lets the C++ fallback share them: they use is_fake_tensor /
  maybe_get_real_tensor / maybe_set_real_tensor instead of
  isinstance(t, FakeTensor) and .real_tensor. Each accessor checks FakeTensor
  first, so Python FakeTensors take the same path as before.
- The real op runs under unset_fake_temporarily(). This is a no-op inside
  __torch_dispatch__, which asserts the fake mode is already unset; it is
  for the C++ fallback calling in.
- Real propagation for register_fake kernels runs after the kernel's
  set_ctx_getter/fake-mode context exits rather than inside it, as it already
  did for the MissingOpProfile path and the other branches. Propagation
  doesn't depend on that context: the one step that needs the fake mode
  (_infer_fake_from_real_tensor) enters it itself.

_dispatch_impl checks for a registered fake kernel before calling
run_fake_impl, so whatever the kernel returns, including NotImplemented, is
propagated and returned as before. run_fake_impl's own NotImplemented only
means "no kernel registered".

```bash
lintrunner -a torch/_subclasses/fake_tensor.py torch/_library/fake_impl.py
```

[CPP FakeTensor] Keep C++ fakes out of plain-tensor-only paths (#200136)

Several places use `type(t) is torch.Tensor` (or similar) to mean "a plain,
real tensor". A C++ fake's exact type is torch.Tensor, so it passes these
checks and goes down paths that need real data. meta_utils' _safe_copy and
_safe_clone would copy or clone a fake source into the shadow real tensor,
Tensor.__format__ would call .item() on a 0-dim fake, the DDP SubmodCompiler's
"output should be fake or subclass" assertion would reject C++ fake outputs,
the optests _clone_input_for_aot_autograd helper would ask a fake whether
it is pinned, which needs real storage, and torch._C._is_cow_tensor (with
Dynamo's _try_is_cow_tensor guard helper) would read a fake's storage data
pointer.

Each check additionally excludes torch._C._is_fake_tensor / is_fake_tensor
(Tensor::is_fake() in C++),
which is false for every tensor unless a C++ fake exists, so there is no
change for Python FakeTensor.

FakeTensorConverter.from_real_tensor reads a 0-dim CPU tensor's value with
.item() to memoize it; a C++ fake passes _is_plain_tensor, so it is excluded
with is_fake().

[CPP FakeTensor] Add fake tensor accessor helpers (#193750)

C++ fake tensors are plain torch.Tensor objects, so code that reaches into
Python FakeTensor attributes (fake_device, item_memo, constant, real_tensor,
dispatch_keys) or checks isinstance(x, FakeTensor) silently skips them. This
adds maybe_get_*/maybe_set_* helpers in fake_tensor.py that handle both kinds
(plus the _clear_fake_real_tensor binding they need), and switches
fake_tensor.py itself over to them and to is_fake_tensor. The following
commits in the stack switch the rest of torch over, one file or folder at a
time.

This is intended to be a refactor for today's (Python FakeTensor) behavior:
every new C++ branch is gated on torch._C._is_fake_tensor, which is false for
every tensor unless a C++ fake exists. Equivalences worth checking when
reviewing:

- merge_devices reads the fake device directly instead of t.device. All
  _find_common_device callers run outside in_kernel_invocation, where
  FakeTensor.device already returns fake_device.
- allow_non_fake_inputs_temporarily is added here as a replacement for
  mock.patch.object(mode, "allow_non_fake_inputs", True), which cannot
  restore C++-backed properties. allow_non_fake_inputs is a plain instance
  attribute set in __init__ on the Python mode.
- FakeTensorMode.clear_non_cpu_constants forwards to the converter.
